result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend the same variant: Select and Paint as visible modes, with Record as a separate action. Both explain the specific risk of telling a long-press from a drag in a dark booth under stress. A does more to limit mistakes at show time: an undo button that stays on screen, saved cue versions so an overwrite can be rolled back, specific confirmations, and a blind or preview step before painted changes reach the stage. B adds a useful show-lock and a hold-to-paint fallback, but its 'revert on lift' rule is underspecified. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers make the same core choice: Select and Paint as visible modes, with Record as a separate, deliberate action. Both also explain clearly why timing-based gestures fail under show pressure. B is somewhat stronger on reversing wrong-mode mistakes: undo stays on screen, cue versions can be rolled back, paint is set before the drag so a gesture never means two things, and a live/blind staging step keeps paint errors off the stage. A's strengths are a show-lock and an explicit fallback (a hold-to-paint button) if switching modes turns out to be too slow.
